items.body_html: every T1 datum is written to durable storage during the run, not at teardown — the record is born durable, not rescued later
no T1/T3 datum has its only copy in the runtime workspace (T4); the canonical record never depends on the workspace surviving

items.name_html: INV-3 · evidence-ref discipline (the one new runtime rule)
items.body_html: a canonical record ref resolves inline (T1) or into the durable evidence store (T3) — never into T4 (evidence_ref_ok). This is the rule whose absence is the v1 evidence-loss bug

a materialized current-state projection is authoritative only if reconstructable/consistent from T1, or it is a sealed snapshot anchored to T1 (projection_authoritative); the runtime workspace is never the only truth

items.name_html: INV-5 · release safety (the bridge to LC2)
items.body_html: no canonical-record ref points into a resource being released (release_safe). LC1 guarantees this by construction (canonical never homes in T4); LC2 Teardown only asserts it, fail-closed
